tweets.text:
This week decides if the whole market goes flying.

Clarity Act cloture vote on the 15th. Warsh's Fed on the 16th. Bank of Japan on the 18th.

Here is what is actually priced in, and what is not...
tweets.hook: This week decides if the whole market goes flying.

tweets.text:
The Fed: a 25 bps hike is about 85% priced in.

Core CPI just printed 2.4% year over year, the lowest since March 2021. Headline is 3.4% because gasoline ran 3.9% in August.

Everyone is pricing Warsh like he is Powell.

Warsh reads through energy. Powell hiked into headline for years and the market learned that reflex.

If Warsh looks at core at 2.4% and holds, everything positioned for a hike has to reprice at once. $BTC first.

The Clarity Act: cloture vote Sept 15, 60 votes needed, Republicans hold 53.

Polymarket has passage in 2026 at 16%, down from 82% in February. Banks and a bloc of Democrats are pushing back.

A pass is the biggest bullish catalyst on the board.

The bear stack: AI stocks dumped on Sept 14 after Amodei, Altman and Musk asked the industry to slow down, and the Bank of Japan is expected to hike to 1.25%.

None of that takes $BTC back near the $57.7K July low.

$KAS just showed how fast a comeback happens: +33% in a month, poked above its 50-week SMA when that looked close to impossible.

$BTC has been sitting on its own 50-week SMA for weeks. A hold plus a Clarity pass and it clears the line.

The four-year cycle zombies want an October bottom. Everyone piling back in around October 1 is exactly why October turns green instead.

Follow me for macro takes that ignore the four-year cycle echo chamber 💪

yt_posts.topic: This week decides if the market goes flying: Fed, Clarity Act, Bank of Japan, and the October zombies
yt_posts.body_style: macro calendar breakdown: Fed reflex under Warsh, Clarity odds, the bear stack, the October zombie read, Kaspa and BTC at the 50-week SMA
yt_posts.body:
This week decides if the whole market goes flying, and almost nobody is pricing the version where it does.

Look at the calendar. September 15: the Senate holds a cloture vote on the Clarity Act. September 16: Warsh's Fed decides on rates. September 18: the Bank of Japan decides, with a hike to 1.25% expected. All of that inside five days, and the crowd has already decided how it ends.

Start with the Fed. A 25 bps hike is about 85% priced in, and since 2007 the Fed has almost always done what the market priced this strongly. Here is the catch: that reflex was learned under Powell, and Powell is gone. Core CPI just printed 2.4% year over year, the lowest since March 2021. Headline CPI is 3.4%, and gasoline alone was over a third of the monthly increase. Warsh has said out loud that he reads through energy. So everyone is pricing Warsh like he is Powell, and if he looks at core at 2.4% and holds, everything positioned for a hike has to reprice at once. Bitcoin first.

Then the Clarity Act. Cloture needs 60 votes and Republicans hold 53, so it needs seven crossovers, and a bloc of Democrats plus the banks are pushing back. Polymarket has passage in 2026 at 16%, down from 82% in February. Two weeks ago I did not think it would even get a vote, so the fact that it is on the floor at all is progress. If it passes, that is the biggest bullish catalyst on the board.

Now the bear stack, because it is real. AI stocks dumped on September 14 after Amodei, Altman and Musk spent the weekend asking the industry to slow down, and the whole stock market has been riding the AI trade. Add a Bank of Japan hike and you get the four-year cycle zombies screaming for a new bottom. They want it in October, because the cycle says so. My read: a September dip does not take Bitcoin anywhere near the $57.7K July low, and the zombies never get their October bottom, because everyone piling back in around October 1 is exactly what turns October green.

And the chart already gave a preview. $KAS ran 33% in a month and poked above its 50-week SMA when that looked close to impossible. Bitcoin has been sitting on its own 50-week SMA for weeks. A hold plus a Clarity pass and it clears the line, and the bull market is on. Even one of the two is enough.

Never financial advice. Never.

So commit in the comments: does Warsh hike on the 16th and we dip, or does he hold and we fly? And if you think the Clarity Act is what actually decides the week, say that instead.

Hit like and subscribe if you want macro takes that ignore the four-year cycle echo chamber.

yt_posts.topic: The stonk narrative in three steps: memes paired with tokenized stocks, holder rewards, then $TAO pairs
yt_posts.body_style: narrative arc: three-step evolution of stock-paired meme coins, the launchpad numbers, Mike's take, the community 90x
yt_posts.body:
Meme coins stopped pairing with SOL, and in about two months the stonk narrative went from a gimmick to $TAO paired memes and a $140 million launchpad token.

Stonk is just crypto slang for stock, and the stonk narrative is the intersection of the crypto market and the stock market: tokenized real-world stocks meeting meme coin culture. Here is how it evolved, step by step.

Step one: pair the meme with a tokenized stock. StonkFun on Solana launches new coins paired against xStocks like NVDAx and SPYx, and pre-IPO tokens like OPENAI and ANTHROPIC, instead of the usual SOL or USDC pair. The meme's dollar price now moves with the stock and with the meme at the same time. Over the first weekend of September the platform moved its launches onto Raydium LaunchLab, and xStocks took over 40% of the launches.

Step two: pay the holders in the paired asset. Some of these launches now route trading volume into rewards for holders, paid in the asset the coin is paired with. Hold the meme, get paid in the stock. That is a completely different reason to hold a meme coin than a picture of a dog.

Step three: pair it with a real crypto. Not just layer ones. ZEC, HYPE and $TAO are now the biggest crypto-paired buckets on the launchpad, so you can hold a meme and collect exposure to Bittensor instead of NVIDIA. That is where this landed in two months.

The numbers: STONK, the launchpad's own token, ran to a $140 million market cap on September 6 with about $135 million of daily volume. That is not a niche.

My take: the coins that pay rewards are going to be the ones people actually want to hold, because holding pays you in something you already wanted. I have seen the same sentiment everywhere; people are genuinely excited about the idea. Plenty of these retrace 50% first, and some will rug, so entries matter more than the narrative. Never financial advice. Never.

And one buy alert in my community did a 90x this week while the US was asleep: Perps Pad, now sitting around a $7 million market cap. This is the kind of week we are having.

So tell me straight in the comments: if you had to hold one meme for the rest of the year, do you want the one paired with NVIDIA or the one paired with $TAO? And if you think the whole stonk narrative is a top signal, say that too.

Hit like and subscribe if you want to hear about these narratives before they hit the timeline.

That is the whole lesson of this move. A coin that everyone wrote off in the bear market can make a real comeback, and it can do it fast. Kaspa is a fully implemented GhostDAG on proof of work, fair launched, no premine, and the market is finally remembering it.

3.4 cents, still under a billion dollar market cap. The weekly close above the 50-week SMA is a matter of when 💪
